Finding 03 / coordination

Presence is not correctness

Available supervision prevented stale work, then introduced a defect of its own.

Research noteEvidence pack / current programmeQualification preserved

A lead must remain available to preserve the mission. Availability improves recovery. It does not make the lead infallible.

What we observed

In a support experiment, causal policy delivery prevented 16 stale outcomes and closed 96 of 96 cases. A terminal-only comparison accepted 80 of 96.

16stale outcomes prevented
1duplicate-case contamination introduced

The supervised run created its own defect. Independent evaluation caught one duplicate-case contamination. The same mechanism that improved recovery did not guarantee correctness.

What changed

The lead remains a distinct, non-producing mission keeper and final judge, even when that adds latency. Consequential acceptance boundaries still need independent outcome checks. Supervision can escalate a concern. It cannot grant itself authority.

What remains open

We still need to learn which checks best generalise across code, research, documents and live operations without turning judgement into a rigid workflow.
